items.q: R-Font is the second one. Piku, well that's the family.

ctx.x: I got it from him last year.

My Godfather used to be a great undertaker on Ramport and... Well, this street here... Well, they changed the two names. No. Governor Nichols. Governor Nichols. But it wasn't Governor Nichols at that time. Hospital. Hospital. Okay, I guess it's going again. You were talking about your... Your Godfather that lived on the hospital street. Yeah. Yeah. And... He gave me his name. Floreston is my first name. R-Font is the second one. Piku, well that's the family. You see? But I changed that Floreston because I had so…
Do you have any... Do you remember... When was the first time that you can remember that people were using the word jazz?

items.title: Alphonse Picou Interview, 1958-04-04
items.q: The interviewee discusses 'Albert Burbank' (referred to as 'Burbank') as 'one of my boys' and 'I know that', but the specific mention of 'composer of A La Ba' is linked by the interviewer to Burbank, while the interviewee attributes the composition to his brother. The interviewee does not explicitly

ctx.x: What about Albert Burbank? Oh. Well, Burbank... That's another one. That's one of my boys. Yeah, I know that. Yeah, I know that. Yes. Way back, yeah. That's one of my boys.
I noticed that his name is listed as composer of A La Ba. How does he happen to hold the copyright on that? Do you know?

Who? Who do you think originally wrote A La Ba? Who was the first one to sing? My brother. He's a composer of A La Ba. Your brother. How long ago? Oh, they did some music. And... Did he just write the words or the music? Or both?
